findings.reason: the node dispatched for §4 would either report an unmeasurable before window or silently substitute a shorter one, and the plan needs a snapshot step before §2 lands (or a raised retention cap named in the section) for the measure to be satisfiable at all.
findings.text: §4's measure needs a 24-hour before-window and a 24-hour after-window from `admission-verdicts.jsonl`, but the writer trims the file to 1,048,576 bytes on every append (`trim_service_log(..., limit=ADMISSION_VERDICT_LOG_MAX_BYTES, keep=ADMISSION_VERDICT_LOG_MAX_BYTES)` at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2095-2100); measured today the whole file is 1,046,971 bytes and spans 2026-11-07T05:20 to 2026-11-08T12:14, about 31 hours, so by the time §2 lands and the after-window closes the before-window rows are gone and the fragment can never record both windows

findings.reason: without the declared wait the two sections race on one mechanism, and §5's change is either lost in §2's rewrite or landed twice.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares only `s4: [s2, s3]`, while §5 says "§2 keeps directory claims exclusive, so this blocker survives §2" and therefore edits the same claim logic §2 introduces; the queue orders only what the plan declares, so §5 can launch before §2 and its exception will be re-encoded away by §2's own implementer

findings.reason: a worker told to deliver an existing default and given no call site will spend its gate on the wrong file, or land a second mechanism beside the one that already works.
findings.text: §5 states what must happen but names no module, function or call site, so no caller is identified; the claim check it must alter lives in `runs._raise_live_scope_conflict` / `reckon/crew/runs.py:1574` and is reached through `dispatch_claims.py`, and one of its two deliverables is already present (`_landing_fragment_paths`, reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1068, already defaults a node's fragment to `docs/evidence/fragments/<plan>/<node-id>.html`), leaving the narrowing rule as the only real change
